hook: The great Jewish thinker of the Middle Ages, and doctor at the court of Saladin.

pages.x: Moses ben Maimon was born in Córdoba, in Muslim Spain, in 1138, the son of a rabbi and judge. When he was ten a harsh new dynasty conquered the city and ordered Jews and Christians to convert or leave. His family wandered for years, then settled in Fez in Morocco.

Around 1166 the family reached Cairo. His beloved younger brother David, a jewel trader who supported them all, drowned in the Indian Ocean with the family fortune. Maimonides was too grief-stricken to work for a year, then became a doctor to keep the family.

He became doctor to Saladin's chief minister and the royal court. He described his days: treating courtiers from early morning, then coming home to a waiting room full of Jews and gentiles until night, so tired he could only talk lying down.

In 14 books he set out all of Jewish law, clearly and in order, so that anyone could find what to do without searching the vast Talmud. It took ten years. Some rabbis were furious, but it is still a pillar of Jewish law.

For readers torn between faith and reason, he wrote The Guide for the Perplexed, in Arabic. The Bible and the philosophy of Aristotle, he argued, do not truly clash, and God is beyond anything words can describe. Thomas Aquinas and Spinoza both read it.

Jews say of him: "From Moses to Moses there was none like Moses." He taught that the highest form of charity is to help someone stand on their own feet, with a gift, a loan or a job. He was buried at Tiberias, by the Sea of Galilee.

Maimonides is the most influential Jewish thinker of the Middle Ages. His law code, his Thirteen Principles of Faith and his philosophy still guide Jewish life, and his work bridged Jewish, Muslim and Christian thought.
pts: Wrote the Mishneh Torah, a code of all Jewish law
Wrote The Guide for the Perplexed
Doctor at the court of Saladin
